verified_claims: Verification: for f(x)=x+c (c>=0), the squared right gap (x+y+c)^2-4x(y+c) and the squared left gap 2x^2+2(y+c)^2-(x+y+c)^2 both expand EXACTLY to (x-y-c)^2>=0. Confirmed by symbolic expansion both ways.
Squaring is order-preserving in the verification and in (C1)/(C2) because all quantities (square roots of positive reals, and (f(x)+y)/2 with f(x),y>0) are strictly positive.
c>=0 is necessary: c<0 gives f(x)=x+c<0 for 0<x<-c, violating codomain R_{>0}; c=0 gives f(x)=x>0, c>0 gives f(x)>c>0. So the parameter range is exact.

Step 1: substituting (x,y)=(f(t),t) (valid since f(t),t>0) makes the outer sqrt in (C1) equal sqrt((f(t)^2+f(t)^2)/2)=f(t), and the right sqrt in (C2) equal sqrt(f(t)*f(t))=f(t), so the shared middle term (f(f(t))+t)/2 is squeezed to f(t), yielding f(f(t))=2f(t)-t for all t>0.

Step 2: D(f(t))=f(f(t))-f(t)=(2f(t)-t)-f(t)=D(t); the iterate recurrence a_{n+1}=2a_n-a_{n-1} has characteristic (r-1)^2=0, giving a_n=t+n*D(t) (verified for n=0..6 and by closed-form induction). If D(t)<0 then t+nD(t)->-infty<0, contradicting positivity of every iterate; hence D(t)>=0.

Step 3: completing the square in (C2), (f(u)+v)^2-4uv = (v-(2u-f(u)))^2+4u*D(u) (verified symbolically); dividing by 4u gives D(v)<=D(u)+(v-(2u-f(u)))^2/(4u); setting u=f(s) and using D(f(s))=D(s) and 2f(s)-f(f(s))=s (from (1)) yields D(v)<=D(s)+(v-s)^2/(4f(s)) for all s,v>0.

Step 4: swapping s<->v in (3) (valid since (3) holds for ALL s,v>0) gives D(s)-D(v)<=(v-s)^2/(4f(v)); with f(v)>=v>s/2 near s, both D(v)-D(s) and D(s)-D(v) are <=(v-s)^2/(2s)->0, so D is continuous. No regularity assumed; continuity is derived.

Step 5: on compact [a,b], f continuous & positive => m=min f>0; from (3) and its swap |D(v)-D(s)|<=(v-s)^2/(4m). Partitioning [p,q] into n equal steps and applying the triangle inequality gives |D(q)-D(p)|<=n*((q-p)/n)^2/(4m)=(q-p)^2/(4mn)->0, verified symbolically; hence D(p)=D(q) on [a,b], and since (0,infinity)=union_n[1/n,n], D is constant globally.

Both (C1) and (C2) are used in the proof: (C1) supplies the upper bound in the Step-1 squeeze (and excluding e.g. f=2x which actually satisfies C2 but fails C1 with a large negative gap, confirmed numerically), (C2) supplies the lower bound and the master inequality. No unused/redundant structure.

Numerical re-check (independent of the author): master bound (3) shows zero violations for f=x+c across c in {0,0.5,1,2,5,17.3}; f=x+c satisfies both inequalities (min gap ~0, FP noise only); f=2x violates (C1) badly. Consistent with the analytical proof.
summary: The solution correctly determines the full solution set f(x)=x+c with constant c>=0. The verification is correct and tight: both squared inequalities reduce exactly to (x-y-c)^2>=0 (confirmed by symbolic expansion). The uniqueness proof is rigorous and self-contained with no regularity assumptions: (1) the (f(t),t) substitution squeezes the shared middle term to f(t), forcing the iterate identity f(f(t))=2f(t)-t; (2) the resulting arithmetic-progression iterates t+nD(t) must all stay positive, so D=f-id>=0; (3) completing the square in (C2) and evaluating at u=f(s) yields the quadratic master bound D(v)<=D(s)+(v-s)^2/(4f(s)); (4) this bound plus its swap and f>=id give continuity of D; (5) a uniform (v-s)^2/(4m) bound on compact intervals, telescoped over an n-partition to (q-p)^2/(4mn)->0, forces D constant. I independently re-derived every algebraic identity (symbolic) and confirmed the master bound is tight for f=x+c and that (C1) genuinely excludes non-solutions like f=2x. No fatal gaps, no circularity (continuity is derived from (2)+(3), not assumed), no quantifier changes (all bounds hold for every s,v>0), and the squaring steps are justified by strict positivity. The only non-proof material is clearly-labeled numerical evidence; I re-ran representative checks independently and they agree, but they are non-load-bearing. This is a complete, correct IMO-level proof.
transfer_assessment: REUSABLE — Equality-squeeze substitution (x,y)=(f(t),t): when a two-sided functional inequality has a shared middle term, choosing inputs that collapse one outer bound from each side onto the same value forces the middle to equality. Broadly applicable to functional inequalities (not just equations).

REUSABLE — Iterate/recurrence analysis with positivity: converting a self-composition identity into a linear recurrence on forward orbits, then using a global positivity/range constraint on ALL iterates to sign the drift D(t). Powerful when the codomain is a half-line; turns iteration into a global constraint.

REUSABLE — Quadratic-Lipschitz => constant (partition telescoping): a pointwise bound |g(v)-g(s)|<=C*(v-s)^2 on a compact interval, summed over an n-partition, yields |g(q)-g(p)|<=C'*(q-p)^2/n -> 0, forcing g constant. Classic and very transferable; here the quadratic (rather than linear) modulus is exactly what makes the telescoping vanish.

REUSABLE — Completing the square to localize a global bound: rewriting (f(u)+v)^2-4uv as (v-(2u-f(u)))^2+4u*D(u), then choosing u=f(s) so the shifted center lands exactly at s, turns a global inequality into a local quadratic upper bound on D. A clean localization trick worth remembering.

REUSABLE — Deriving continuity from a two-sided bound before using it: proving continuity of D from the master inequality (rather than assuming f is continuous) is the correct way to handle 'no regularity' hypotheses; this pattern should be reused whenever a problem states no regularity.

NOT MISLEADING — The falsification entries (e.g. rejecting D=k*sqrt(x) via (C1) at y->0) are consistent with the proof: a first-order/local expansion alone is insufficient because the D^2 slack term absorbs first-order constraints; only the global quadratic+partition argument is decisive. Correctly flagged as evidence, not proof.
